evidence_classes.IDENTIFIER: a key, not a claim: a team, a player id, a position, a bucket label
evidence_classes.DISPLAY: the engine's own number, DISPLAYED and never scored here; its accuracy record is the live scorecard's, not this sheet's
evidence_classes.CAPTURED: a measurement read off a committed capture file — what the provider or the contest actually said
evidence_classes.PROVEN: an ACCEPTED research result with support behind it: S-010's stack correlation, use-vs-ignore
evidence_classes.PROXY: a stand-in computed under a STATED assumption the data cannot support, labelled and dated: see the S-015 caveat printed with the table
evidence_classes.UNVALIDATED: a display of a hypothesis that PREDATES ITS TEST. No probability claim, no support yet

sentences.season_rule: S-016, quoted: 'NOTHING in this module compares a 2026 forecast to a 2026 realized outcome — the alpha displays, the sealed season-end protocol scores'. THIS MODULE READS THE LIVE SEASON BY DESIGN and that is owner-directed and DISPLAY ONLY, so there is no locked-season refusal on its display path: a refusal there would refuse the only season there is anything to display. What stands in its place is a SCAN over this module's own source AND its own globals proving that NO READER OF REALIZED OUTCOMES IS NAMED OR BOUND HERE AT ALL — so there is no codepath that could score anything, whatever it was handed. The scan carries teeth: a planted import of a realized-stats reader must be caught, and so must a planted namespace that binds one
sentences.projection_rule: A PROJECTION HERE IS DRAWABLE-PPR AT THE ENGINE'S OWN MEANS: 1.0 x receptions + 0.1 x (receiving + rushing yards) + 0.04 x passing yards + 4 x passing TDs + 6 x anytime TDs, on the live archive's stored means, which is SALIENCE_D D.1 item 3 — the same metric the capture program measures and the same one the boom proxy is read in. IT IS NOT A DRAFTKINGS SCORING PROJECTION: interceptions, fumbles, two-point conversions and return or defensive touchdowns are omitted on both sides, which is the approximation S-015's validation table measured (97-99% agreement for RB/TE/WR, 86% for QB). IT IS DISPLAYED, NEVER SCORED
sentences.ownership_rule: OWNERSHIP IS READ OFF THE COMMITTED SUMMARIES 'research/shape/ownership' AND NOWHERE ELSE — nothing is fetched. THE PROJECTED SHARE IS PREFERRED AT 'projections_t90' AND FALLS BACK TO 'projections_t24', and which one a week used is stated in the sheet. THE JOIN RULE: a summary row the capture RESOLVED joins on its gsis id, and a row it could not resolve joins on its DISPLAY NAME (normalized: lower-cased, stripped of everything but letters, digits and single spaces). EVERY ROW THAT JOINS NEITHER WAY IS COUNTED AND NAMED — unjoined ownership rows in one count, live players with no share in the other — because a join that quietly lost half a slate would read as a slate nobody owned
sentences.name_join_limit: A SCHEMA LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN WORKED AROUND: `live_projections` carries a gsis id but NO DISPLAY NAME column, so the display-name half of the join can only fire on a row that carries one. Until that column exists the unresolved ownership rows cannot be matched to a live player at all, they are COUNTED AS UNJOINED, and a live player with no ownership row is printed by his gsis id, his team and his position. No other surface is consulted for a name: inventing one would be a different join wearing this one's name
sentences.absence_rule: PER-TABLE ABSENCE, S-016: 'an absent ownership file drops the ownership columns for that week, stated in the sheet, never invented'. So a missing summary is NOT a failed run — the columns that needed it print as absent, the sheet SAYS WHICH FILE IT LOOKED FOR AND DID NOT FIND, and the run completes. Only two things make a run INCOMPLETE: no database at all, and no live projections for the week at all — in both cases there is no sheet to draw
sentences.no_bet_footer: THIS SHEET CONTAINS NO BET AND NO PLAY RECOMMENDATION, AND SAYS SO HERE BECAUSE S-016 BINDS A FIXED FOOTER THAT SAYS IT. It is a PRIVATE weekly display for the owner: the engine's own projections beside the captured ownership, each column labelled as what it is. Nothing here is a pick, a play, an edge, a lock, a leverage call or an expected-value claim; no number here has been scored against a 2026 outcome, and the season-end leverage test stays predeclared and untouched. The owner may share his own sheet wherever he likes; THE PROGRAM ITSELF PUBLISHES NOTHING.

rules.text: PER TEAM, OFF THE LIVE PROJECTIONS THEMSELVES, because the live archive carries no consensus mainlines to choose a role on the way S-010 did: THE QB is the teammate with the HIGHEST PROJECTED PASSING YARDS and THE WR1 is the teammate with the HIGHEST PROJECTED RECEIVING YARDS, both strictly above zero ('a priced QB and WR1', S-016), TIES BREAKING ON THE PLAYER ID so the choice is a function of the data and never of row order. THE CHOSEN QB IS EXCLUDED FROM THE WR1 SEARCH, so a stack is always two distinct players — the B pair is a QB's pass leg against ANOTHER player's receiving leg, and a row pairing a player with himself would be a correlation of one. A team missing either leg IS LISTED WITH THE REASON rather than dropped silently

THE WEEK'S GAMES ARE PLACED IN THE S-010 BUCKETS WITH S-010'S OWN CUT VALUES, read out of the committed correlation map and TRANSCRIBED NOWHERE: spread tercile x total tercile, the spread variable being the MAGNITUDE of the T-90 handicap (a game-level number, so both teams of a game land in one bucket) and the total variable the T-90 game total in points. The placing function is `joint_b.tercile_of` BY IMPORT, the same one that built the table. THE LINE IS LOOKED UP BY TEAM in the T-90 bundle and the row records whether the bundle's game id agreed with the archive's. WHERE THE BUCKET IS UNREADABLE — no line for the team, no bucket table, or a bucket the table carries no r for — THE ROW FALLS BACK TO THE POOLED r AND SAYS SO IN ITS OWN NOTE (S-016), and where even the pooled r is unreadable the cell is empty and named as empty. NOTHING IS INVENTED

UNDER-OWNED (S-016): BOTH LEGS BELOW THE SLATE'S MEDIAN OWNERSHIP AT THEIR POSITIONS. The median is taken over THIS WEEK'S live-projection players at that position WHO JOINED AN OWNERSHIP ROW — a position with no joined rows has no median and the flag is NOT COMPUTED for a leg at that position, which is printed as unknown rather than as false. THE FLAG IS UNVALIDATED: it is the display form of the leverage hypothesis and predates its test by design

rules.text: RANKS ARE WITHIN POSITION, 1 = the largest, COMPETITION RANKING: tied values SHARE THE SMALLEST RANK and the next distinct value skips, so two players tied for the top are both rank 1 and the next is rank 3. Ties break on the player id for ordering only, never for the rank itself. THE RANK GAP IS OWNERSHIP RANK MINUS PROJECTION RANK: positive means THE MODEL LIKES HIM MORE THAN THE CROWD DOES. A player the ownership file does not carry has NO ownership rank and NO gap — he is printed with the gap named as absent and sorted after every player who has one, because a missing share is not a low share

rules.text: THE BOOM PROXY IS COMONOTONIC BY ASSUMPTION, STATED: the archive stores each statistic's draws sorted onto its own 21-point grid, so this column sums THE STATS' VALUES AT THE SAME GRID POINT — the world in which a player's every statistic lands at the same quantile at once — and reads the grid point NEAREST THE TOP OF THE CEILING SHARE (the 1 - share mark, on the archive's own declared grid). A stat with no grid stored contributes nothing and the count of stats actually read rides the row

S-015, quoted: 'The live archive's existing 21-point quantile grids are NOT sufficient and are not an accepted alternative: live/archive.py sorts each statistic's draws independently onto its grid, which destroys both the within-player covariance needed to sum drawable-PPR across statistics and the cross-player draw alignment needed to rank a top-15% within one coherent world, so a probability rebuilt from those marginals would calibrate D.2 against a different metric.'

THIS COLUMN IS A PROXY AND IS NEVER PRESENTED AS THE REAL NUMBER. It is NOT a ceiling probability and it is not comparable across players as one. S-016 binds its retirement: the column is REPLACED the week the main session persists draw-aligned ceiling probabilities (or the draw-aligned samples they need) beside live_projections, which is the written request S-015 item 2 put to that thread
